brief.summary_1line: King Dasharatha confesses that his present misery comes from a youthful mistake when he accidentally killed a hermit boy by shooting at a sound.

image_candidates.scene_text: In the dark beside the Sarayu river, Dasharatha releases a poisoned arrow toward a sound, only to hear a wounded youth cry out in the night.
The dying hermit boy lies bleeding on the forest ground beside a spilled water pot, fixing the horrified king with a burning gaze.
Dasharatha stands frozen in the rainy forest as the wounded ascetic youth laments that his blind, thirsty parents are waiting for him.

deep.rich_summary: On the sixth night after Rama’s exile, King Dasharatha awakens tormented by grief and realizes his suffering is the fruit of a past sin. Speaking to Queen Kaushalya, he reflects on karma: one who acts without considering consequences must eventually reap the result. In his youth he prided himself on the skill of shooting by sound alone. While hunting on the banks of the Sarayu during the rainy season, he heard what he believed was an elephant filling itself with water and loosed a poisoned arrow. Instead he struck a young ascetic boy who had come to draw water for his blind, aged parents. The dying youth laments not his own death but the fate of his helpless parents. Dasharatha’s recollection reveals the moral cause of his present anguish and foreshadows the curse and tragic destiny tied to Rama’s exile.

highlight_spans.why: Opening grief of the royal household and Kaushalya’s reflection on the destructive power of sorrow.
Dasharatha’s moral reflection comparing cutting down the mango tree while watering the palasa—an image explaining karmic consequences.
The lush description of the rainy season and natural world before the fateful hunt sets a mythic, atmospheric stage.
The pivotal moment when Dasharatha shoots by sound, believing he has targeted an elephant, triggering the tragic mistake.
The wounded ascetic youth’s lament about his blind parents—an emotional centerpiece that intensifies the moral tragedy.

top_scenes.scene_text: Young Dasharatha in a storm-dark forest by the Sarayu releases a poisoned arrow toward a sound in the darkness as monsoon clouds gather overhead.
The mortally wounded ascetic boy lies on the muddy riverbank beside a fallen water vessel while the shocked prince stands over him with bow slipping from his hands.
Inside the dim palace chamber, the aged Dasharatha awakens in anguish beside Queen Kaushalya, haunted by the memory of the fatal arrow.
